questions.question: A woman who has had three pregnancies, two living children and one miscarriage is:
questions.explanation: Gravida counts all pregnancies; para counts births beyond viability.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The first trimester of pregnancy ends at:
questions.explanation: Second trimester 14–27 weeks; third from 28 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: At 20 weeks of gestation the uterine fundus is palpable at about the level of the:
questions.explanation: At 12 weeks the fundus reaches the symphysis pubis; at 36 weeks the xiphisternum.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Quickening is the first perception by the mother of:

options.C: Fetal movements (about 18–20 weeks in a primigravida)

questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which hormone maintains the corpus luteum in early pregnancy?
questions.explanation: The placenta takes over progesterone production by about 10–12 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Excess amniotic fluid (polyhydramnios) is associated with:

options.B: Maternal diabetes and fetal oesophageal atresia or anencephaly

questions.explanation: Oligohydramnios is associated with renal agenesis and growth restriction.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which drug is a known teratogen causing neural tube defects?
questions.explanation: Others: warfarin, ACE inhibitors, isotretinoin, thalidomide.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Hyperemesis gravidarum is:

options.D: Severe persistent vomiting in pregnancy with weight loss and dehydration

questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A hydatidiform mole classically presents with:

options.C: Bleeding, a uterus larger than dates and a ‘snowstorm’ ultrasound appearance

questions.explanation: Very high hCG; treat by suction evacuation.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Anti-D immunoglobulin is given to Rh-negative mothers:

options.D: Within 72 hours after delivery of an Rh-positive baby and at 28 weeks

questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Preterm labour is defined as labour before:
questions.explanation: Corticosteroids are given to accelerate fetal lung maturity.

questions.question: Complications more common in twin pregnancy include:
questions.explanation: Monochorionic twins risk twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Shoulder dystocia is most associated with:
questions.explanation: May cause Erb's palsy or clavicle fracture.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An absolute indication for caesarean section is:

options.D: Twin pregnancy with cephalic first twin

questions.explanation: Also cephalopelvic disproportion and transverse lie.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Episiotomy is:

options.D: A surgical incision of the perineum to enlarge the vaginal outlet

questions.question: In neonatal resuscitation, the most important first step is:

options.D: Clearing the airway and providing ventilation

questions.explanation: Chest compressions begin if heart rate <60 despite ventilation.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Delayed cord clamping in term neonates for 1–3 minutes:

options.D: Improves iron stores and haemoglobin in the infant

questions.question: Postpartum ‘blues’ typically:

questions.question: Breastfeeding is contraindicated in a mother who is:
